label: assertion
text: Complexity regularization that satisfies Norton's Material Theory of Induction (MTI) by localizing the inductive risk to local facts in the given domain — exemplified by the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) and its iterative magnitude pruning (IMP) — provides an epistemic justification for inductive generalizations learned by overparameterized artificial neural networks. Unlike global uniformities such as simplicity or compression, MTI-based regularization avoids epistemic circularity because the inductive risk is transferred from a generic schema to the actual local facts present in the training data, making the resulting generalization epistemically justifiable without appealing to non-local facts.

label: assertion
text: For overparameterized neural networks, Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) can suffer from a No-Go-ERM trivialization (【2, 8】).

label: assertion
text: For overparameterized neural networks, the two-sided uniform convergence of empirical risk to risk fails.

label: 论据
text: For overparameterized neural networks, both data-distribution-independent bounds (based on Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) dimension) and data-distribution-dependent bounds (based on weight norms) become uninformative.

label: assertion
text: That the two-sided uniform convergence of empirical risk to risk fails results in the absence of asymptotic stability of Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM).

label: assertion
text: For overparameterized neural networks, the collapse of Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) to trivialization can be blocked by adopting a local stability provided by the Material Theory of Induction (MTI).

label: assertion
text: The strengths of inductive support for Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) are derived from the local context rather than from a global asymptotic requirement.

label: assertion
text: For overparameterized neural networks, the Material Theory of Induction (MTI) replaces the unavailable asymptotic uniform convergence of empirical risk to risk with a strictly local convergence of empirical risk to risk.

label: assertion
text: For overparameterized neural networks, local stability of Empirical Risk Minimization under the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis is achieved when iterative magnitude pruning identifies matching subnetworks (as defined in 【11, 12, 13, 14】) that are robust to stochastic gradient descent noise.

label: assertion
text: Robustness to stochastic gradient descent (SGD) noise is characterized by linear mode connectivity (see 【7, 8】).

label: assertion
text: At each round \(n\) of iterative magnitude pruning (IMP), if the axial subspace defined by the refined pruning mask \(m_{n+1}\) (see 【16】) intersects the epsilon-linearly connected sublevel set (LCSS; see 【10】) of the current weights \(W_n\), then rewinding the remaining weights to their values at an early training step \(k\) (obtaining \(W_k\)) and training the subnetwork \(f(X; m_{n+1} \odot W_k)\) to convergence produces updated weights \(W_{n+1}\) that are linearly mode-connected to \(W_n\) (see 【7, 8】) and have test error within \(\epsilon\) of the original dense network \(f(X; W)\).

label: assertion
text: The geometric condition in 【15】 is necessary and sufficient for iterative magnitude pruning (IMP) to find a matching subnetwork (as defined in 【11, 12, 13, 14】) at round \(n\).

label: assertion
text: The geometric condition in 【15】 provides the local stability that de-trivializes Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM).

label: assertion
text: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis has been empirically confirmed for neural network architectures used in natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, as well as for pre-trained models.

label: 论据
text: Winning subnetworks (sparse subnetworks that, when their weights are reset to their initial values, can be trained to match the test accuracy of the original dense network) or matching subnetworks (sparse subnetworks found by iterative magnitude pruning with weight rewinding that achieve test accuracy within a small tolerance of the dense network) were successfully identified in the neural network architectures used in natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, as well as for pre-trained models.

label: assertion
text: Pruning based on the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis localizes inductive risk by adapting the network's structure to local facts in each domain—natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning—as well as for pre-trained models.

label: assertion
text: Pruning based on the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis validates the Material Theory of Induction framework across different contexts—natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning—as well as for pre-trained models.

label: assertion
text: The epistemic justification provided by Material Theory of Induction -based complexity regularization holds only when the training data are independent and identically distributed from a fixed distribution and the local facts remain stable across the training and deployment domains.

label: assertion
text: If these conditions—that the training data are independent and identically distributed from a fixed distribution and that the local facts remain stable across the training and deployment domains—are violated, the Material Theory of Induction (MTI) justification fails.

label: assertion
text: If these conditions—that the training data are independent and identically distributed from a fixed distribution and that the local facts remain stable across the training and deployment domains—are violated, the inductive risk must be managed by a different type of justification from the Material Theory of Induction (MTI) justification—specifically, optimality-based meta-induction.

label: assertion
text: Optimality-based meta-induction does not require assumptions about data uniformity.

label: assertion
text: In machine learning, there is a division of labor.

label: assertion
text: The Material Theory of Induction (MTI) provides local justification when data are stationary.

label: assertion
text: Optimality-based meta-induction justifications provide global justification for model selection under non-stationary conditions.
